title: Echo Grid — voice + screen share (LiveKit token exchange + presence)
description: Voice and screen share media never flow through the EchoGrid server. Media goes directly between the client's livekit-client SDK and the LiveKit sidecar SFU. The messages in this schema are the presence + token-exchange handshake that rides the main /ws WebSocket.

voiceJoin.description: Client -> server: join presence for this voice channel. Does not by itself connect to LiveKit — the client follows up with voice.request_token.

voiceLeave.description: Client -> server: leave current voice channel. Client also disconnects from the LiveKit Room.

voicePeerJoined.description: Server -> everyone-in-channel: a peer joined the voice channel.

voiceSpeaking.description: Server -> everyone-in-channel: speaking-state echo driven by LiveKit ActiveSpeakersChanged on the sharer's client.

voiceState.description: Server -> client: full snapshot of current voice-channel membership after (re)join. Fields mirror EchoGrid.Protocol/VoiceMessages.cs.

voiceRequestToken.description: Client -> server: mint me a LiveKit JWT for this voice channel's Room.

voiceToken.description: Server -> client: here is the LiveKit JWT + URL. role is 'publisher' when the caller has Speak permission, otherwise 'subscriber'. The same Room is used for screen share — no second token is ever minted.

voiceReplaced.description: Server -> displaced-session unicast: this session's voice attendance was taken over by another session of the same identity on a different device (voice is device-exclusive per identity; chat, DMs, presence, and typing remain multi-session). The receiving client disconnects from LiveKit and clears local voice state but keeps its chat WebSocket open. reason is a short machine-readable code — currently 'another_device'.

screenRequestToken.description: Client -> server: grant me screen publish permission on my existing voice Room. Caller must already be in the voice channel. Server verifies StartScreenShare, claims the one-sharer-per-channel slot, and calls LiveKit UpdateParticipant to add SCREEN_SHARE / SCREEN_SHARE_AUDIO to canPublishSources.

screenPermissionGranted.description: Server -> caller: publish permission has been flipped on your existing LiveKit participant record. Open the OS picker and publish.

screenStopRequest.description: Client -> server: I am stopping my screen share. Server revokes the publish permission via UpdateParticipant and releases the slot.

screenStarted.description: Server -> everyone-in-channel: someone started sharing their screen on this voice channel.

screenStopped.description: Server -> everyone-in-channel: the sharer stopped (explicit stop_request, leave, or LiveKit webhook-driven release).
